newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Klima keeps Creditanstalt options open.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Klima keeps Creditanstalt options open.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima on Friday said he would invite new bids for privatisation candidate Creditanstalt if a last-minute offer by a group around Austro-Italian insurer EA-Generali failed to meet his demands.
"We would have to search for new bidders on very short notice," Klima told Austrian state television ORF.
A consortium of bidders led by Austro-Italian insurer EA-Generali earlier on Friday said it submitted an offer for the government's 70 percent voting stake in midnight deadline expired.
Klima extended his original deadline by a week and threatened to reopen the six-year long privatisation process to other potential bidders on Monday if the consortium failed to make a bid on time.
The group's final offer was delayed by mounting dissent among its members over a plan by erstwhile consortium member Die Erste to form a joint holding with Creditanstalt, which it would control.

Other consortium members, among them Commerzbank of Germany and Banca Commerciale Italiana, had voiced increasing concern about Die Erste's controlling position in the proposed structure since the savings bank is barely a third of the size of Creditanstalt, Austria's number-two bank.
